summary: DAY adversarial review independently challenged every company in Chief's 12-name active T0 batch using cumulative still-valid primary evidence and the current 21:00Z machine state. No new evidence creates a lane-specific methodology blocker for any of the 12. All are red-team ready_for_chief with explicit concentration, financing, execution, regulatory, substitution and narrative-overreach risks preserved. Readiness is not endorsement and does not override global T0 fail-closed conditions.

companies.redTeamCase: Strategic partners and committed demand can produce false comfort because multi-gigawatt infrastructure must still earn acceptable returns. Meta/NVIDIA/Palantir validation does not prove utilization, gross margin or ROIC; concentration and funding intensity remain the dominant failure path.
falsifiers: material delay/cancellation of committed capacity
capex rises materially faster than contracted gross profit and operating cash generation
financing terms deteriorate as buildout expands
partner channels fail to diversify paying demand

companies.redTeamCase: RPO and recurring imagery demand can obscure satellite replacement capex, government timing and financing/dilution. Liquidity reduces immediate survival risk but does not neutralize constellation-refresh economics.
falsifiers: RPO conversion weakens materially
replacement capex rises faster than gross-profit growth
financing expands share count without corresponding cash-generation improvement

companies.redTeamCase: Category leakage remains the principal narrative trap: Atomic Alchemy's NRC material license is not Aurora commercial-reactor approval, and framework agreements are not bankable generation revenue. Licensing, fuel, project finance and contract conversion remain unresolved execution dependencies.
falsifiers: Aurora licensing milestones slip materially
framework counterparties fail to convert into binding economic agreements
project economics require structurally more capital/dilution than expected

companies.redTeamCase: The Malaysia AI offtake improves forward demand visibility but can be overread. More than $800M expected revenue is multi-year and begins in 2027; targeted customer prepayments covering more than 50% of associated capex still leave residual funding, margin, counterparty and execution risk. Mining beta remains relevant until AI cash flow dominates.
falsifiers: A102 energization/service commencement slips
offtake customers fail to perform or margins disappoint
residual capex/financing produces substantial dilution
self-mining capital needs continue to dominate cash use

companies.redTeamCase: Manufacturing milestones, updated guidance and quantum-security wins are real but unusually easy to extrapolate into a fully validated quantum-computing business. Acquisition complexity and roadmap dependence remain substantial; product milestones cannot substitute for repeatable fault-tolerant economics.
falsifiers: Superion deliveries slip materially or fail to produce repeatable commercial economics
post-acquisition burn remains high without margin progression
integration creates repeated restructuring/impairment or large dilution
security/networking wins remain isolated

companies.redTeamCase: Extreme principal-customer concentration means backlog and deployment visibility can create false comfort. Walmart-linked cadence, receivables and bargaining power should dominate concentration penalties until other customers become material.
falsifiers: principal-customer deployments pause or economics are renegotiated
concentration stays extreme while margins weaken
new customers fail to become material contributors

companies.redTeamCase: AI/custom-silicon enthusiasm can hide direct-customer, distributor and receivable concentration plus cyclicality/export exposure. Design wins should not receive full thesis credit until diversified revenue and cash conversion are visible.
falsifiers: major customer/distributor loss
custom-AI concentration rises while gross margin/cash conversion weakens
export controls materially shrink addressable demand

companies.redTeamCase: AI-optics growth remains exposed to hyperscaler concentration, optical-cycle duration and leverage. Current pricing/yield gains may be cyclical rather than durable moat evidence; debt lowers tolerance for a sharp demand reset.
falsifiers: AI datacenter growth decelerates sharply
top-customer concentration rises with inventory/receivable stress
deleveraging stalls during margin compression

companies.redTeamCase: Debt equitization improves leverage but share issuance is economically real. Hyperscaler concentration plus 1.6T/CPO transitions create upside and obsolescence risk; per-share economics must be normalized rather than celebrating margin acceleration alone.
falsifiers: share-count growth remains material
CPO transition disintermediates current product economics
major-customer concentration rises while margins normalize downward

companies.redTeamCase: Strong margins/cash flow can obscure channel and geographic concentration. Distributor receivables, Taiwan/China exposure and outsourced manufacturing remain dependencies rather than owned moat.
falsifiers: channel inventory correction causes disproportionate revenue decline
Taiwan/China disruption materially constrains supply/end demand
300mm expansion fails qualification or creates persistent cost drag

companies.redTeamCase: Rapid AI-infrastructure growth with high customer concentration creates peak-cycle risk. Revenue acceleration must be separated from margin durability, working-capital intensity and hyperscaler bargaining power.
falsifiers: top-customer growth reverses
working-capital/capex needs consume cash despite revenue growth
operating margin retraces as mix normalizes

companies.redTeamCase: Diversification is genuine, but the acquisition wave creates integration, debt, synergy and capital-allocation risk. Acquired growth should not be mistaken for organic moat expansion without realized returns.
falsifiers: integration costs/synergy realization miss materially
leverage remains elevated while organic growth slows
large acquisitions reduce return on invested capital

contradictions: Validated demand at NBIS and SYM can increase concentration and execution risk rather than reduce it.
BTDR forward AI offtake reduces demand uncertainty without proving present economics or removing mining-cycle dependence.
IONQ milestones reduce specific technical/commercial uncertainty while increasing the risk of roadmap over-capitalization.
OKLO isotope-license progress is adjacent execution evidence, not reactor-licensing evidence.
APH diversification lowers customer concentration while acquisition intensity raises leverage/integration risk.
unknowns: Exact live crowding, short interest and consensus positioning are non-canonical T0 inputs and are not fabricated.
Future regulatory, technology-transition and renewal outcomes remain falsifiers rather than present blockers unless sourced contradictions emerge.
peerRequests: Chief: all 12 active-batch names are red-team ready_for_chief, but readiness is not endorsement; preserve explicit concentration, capital-structure, integration and cycle penalties.
Underwriting: retain conservative treatment of OKLO framework economics, BTDR forward offtake economics and IONQ post-acquisition normalization.
Expectations-execution: treat NBIS/IONQ/OKLO/BTDR as highly narrative-sensitive and COHR/LITE/CLS/MRVL as AI-cycle-expectation sensitive without contaminating Earth Score.
